The memory bank indicates the root cause is a **double-destruction bug**: CustomHeapManager's destructor is called twice - once explicitly at line 177 in shutdown(), and again at line 186 when ~Application() calls shutdown(). This causes a double-free of heap_memory.

Your current hypothesis about static libstdc++ objects is a different issue. The actual problem is that when the Application object goes out of scope in main(), ~Application() runs and calls shutdown() a second time, attempting to free already-freed memory.

The fix must prevent the second destructor call from executing on already-freed memory. Since you can only modify user.cpp, you need to intervene in the lifecycle to prevent double-destruction - not initialize stdlib features early.
